underTheHoodPage.metaDescription: Learn how AltSendme enables direct peer-to-peer file transfers with tickets, iroh, QUIC encryption, NAT traversal, and open-source relays — no accounts or IP addresses required.
underTheHoodPage.title: Under The Hood
underTheHoodPage.intro: It's like scp without needing to know the IP address. Add some files to AltSendme, and it will give you a pastable ticket that you can give to anyone who needs your files. AltSendme will connect your devices directly & transfer the data without any accounts or configuration.

blobs.title: Blobs
blobs.intro: Content-addressed blob storage and transfer. iroh-blobs implements request/response and streaming transfers of arbitrary-sized byte blobs, using BLAKE3-verified streams and content-addressed links.

items.blob: Blob: an opaque sequence of bytes (no embedded metadata).
items.link: Link: a 32-byte BLAKE3 hash that identifies a blob.
items.hashSeq: HashSeq: a blob that contains a sequence of links (useful for chunking/trees).
items.provider: Provider / Requester: provider serves data; requester fetches it. An endpoint can be both.

tickets.title: Tickets
tickets.body: Tickets are a way to share dialing information between iroh endpoints. They're a single token that contains everything needed to connect to another endpoint, or to fetch a blob in this case. Contains Ed25519 NodeIds: Your device's cryptographic identity for authentication. They're also very powerful. It's worth pointing out this setup is considerably better than full peer-2-peer systems, which broadcast your IP to peers. Instead in iroh, tickets are used to form a "cozy network" between peers you explicitly want to connect with. It's possible to go "full p2p" & configure your app to broadcast dialing details, but tickets represent a better middle-ground default.

peerDiscovery.title: Peer Discovery, NAT Traversal & Hole Punching
peerDiscovery.body: Peers register with an open-source public relay servers at startup to help traverse firewalls and NATs, enabling connection setup. Once connected, iroh uses QUIC hole punching to try and establish a direct peer-to-peer connection, bypassing the relay. If direct connection is possible, communication happens directly between peers with end-to-end encryption; otherwise, the relay operates only temporarily as a fallback. This enables smooth reliable connections between peers within local-network and across the internet.

quic.title: QUIC & Encryption
quic.intro: QUIC is a modern transport protocol built on UDP, designed to reduce latency and improve web performance over TCP. Developed originally by Google and now standardized by the IETF as HTTP/3's foundation, it integrates TLS 1.3 encryption directly into the protocol.

powers.zeroRtt: zero round trip time connection establishment if you've connected to another endpoint before

relays.title: Relays
relays.body: AltSendme uses open-source public relay servers to support establishing direct connections, to speed up initial connection times, and to provide a fallback should direct connections between two endpoints fail or be impossible otherwise. All connections are end-to-end encrypted. The relay is "just another UDP socket" for sending encrypted packets around. <link>Read more</link>.

faq1.question: What is AltSendme and how does it work?
faq1.answer: AltSendme is an open-source peer-to-peer file transfer app for desktop, Android, web, and CLI. It lets you send files and folders anywhere in the world with no accounts and no cloud storage. It is built on the <link>Iroh networking stack</link> and uses ticket-based sharing with NAT hole punching and encrypted relay fallback.

faq2.question: Is AltSendme free to use?
faq2.answer: Yes. AltSendme is free and open source (AGPL-3.0) with no file size limits, no upload quotas, and no accounts. If you benefit from this work, consider supporting development through Buy Me a Coffee or GitHub Sponsors.

faq3.question: What file types can I transfer with AltSendme?
faq3.answer: You can transfer anything—images, videos, documents, folders, and more. Integrity checks use BLAKE3 on both ends, so files are verified during send and receive. Transfers are resumable if interrupted.

faq4.question: How secure is my data when using AltSendme?
faq4.answer: AltSendme uses end-to-end encryption with QUIC + TLS 1.3. Files go directly between devices and are not stored on a cloud server. Relays only see encrypted traffic. Tickets authenticate the intended sender before a transfer starts.

faq5.question: How does AltSendme compare to FilePizza, Wormhole, and PairDrop?
faq5.answer: Unlike browser-only WebRTC tools, AltSendme is a native app (plus Android, web, and CLI) built on Iroh/QUIC. You can send large files and full folders with pause/resume, fewer browser limits, and BLAKE3-verified streaming. See our <compareLink>full comparison</compareLink> for details.

faq6.question: Do I need an internet connection to use AltSendme?
faq6.answer: A network connection is required so devices can reach each other. On the same LAN/Wi-Fi, full internet is not required. Across different networks, internet is used for hole punching or encrypted relay fallback—so AltSendme works over the internet, not only on local Wi-Fi.

faq7.question: Is AltSendme a LocalSend alternative for the internet?
faq7.answer: Yes. LocalSend is excellent for nearby devices on the same local network. AltSendme is built for the same frictionless feel across any network—local or across the internet—using Iroh tickets, QUIC encryption, and optional relays. Compare them on our <compareLink>LocalSend comparison page</compareLink>.

faq8.question: Is AltSendme an open-source Blip alternative?
faq8.answer: Yes. AltSendme is a free, open-source Blip alternative: unlimited file size, no accounts, end-to-end encrypted peer-to-peer transfers, and apps for Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, and the web. See <compareLink>AltSendme vs Blip</compareLink>.

localsend.metaDescription: AltSendme is a LocalSend alternative that works over the internet—not just the same Wi-Fi. Open-source P2P with Iroh gigabit speeds, tickets, Android, web, and CLI.
localsend.title: LocalSend alternative for the internet
localsend.lead: LocalSend is excellent for nearby devices on the same network. AltSendme keeps that frictionless feel across the internet—and adds Iroh/QUIC networking that can saturate gigabit links, plus a real CLI compatible with sendme.
localsend.whenLocalsend1: Both devices are on the same Wi-Fi or LAN
localsend.whenLocalsend2: You want automatic nearby device discovery
localsend.whenLocalsend3: You do not need internet-wide transfers
localsend.whenAltsendme1: Devices are on different networks or across the internet
localsend.whenAltsendme2: You want ticket-based sharing and Iroh speeds that can fill a gigabit pipe
localsend.whenAltsendme3: You need CLI/sendme interop, resumable large folders, or a web app
localsend.faq1q: Does LocalSend work over the internet?
localsend.faq1a: LocalSend is designed for local network transfers between nearby devices. AltSendme is built for both local and internet transfers via Iroh hole punching and relays.
localsend.faq2q: Is AltSendme open source like LocalSend?
localsend.faq2a: Yes. AltSendme is AGPL-3.0 open source, free, with no accounts or upload limits.
localsend.faq3a: Yes. AltSendme is interoperable with the official Iroh sendme CLI—tickets work across GUI and terminal. It also supports Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, and a web app.

blip.metaDescription: AltSendme is a free, open-source Blip alternative. Unlimited P2P with CLI, Iroh gigabit speeds, no accounts, and apps for Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, and web.
blip.title: Open-source Blip alternative
blip.lead: Blip is a popular proprietary large-file transfer app. AltSendme is the open-source alternative: unlimited size, no accounts, a real CLI, end-to-end encrypted P2P on Iroh that can saturate gigabit connections, and full transparency under AGPL-3.0.
blip.whenBlip1: You already rely on Blip’s proprietary workflow
blip.whenBlip2: You prefer a closed commercial product
blip.whenAltsendme1: You want open source you can audit and self-host relays for
blip.whenAltsendme2: You need free unlimited transfers, CLI/sendme interop, and no account lock-in
blip.whenAltsendme3: You want Iroh networking that can push multi-gigabit on a good path
blip.faq1q: Is there a free open-source Blip alternative?
blip.faq1a: Yes. AltSendme is free and open source, with unlimited peer-to-peer transfers, CLI support, and no cloud storage of your files.
blip.faq2a: No. Drop a file, share a ticket, and transfer directly—no signup. Use the GUI or the sendme-compatible CLI.
blip.faq3a: Yes. Transfers use QUIC + TLS 1.3 on Iroh. Relays only forward encrypted packets, and native transfers can saturate gigabit links.
